about.title: People of the AI labs, 1955 to 2026
about.description: Who worked where and when, why they left, how they were tied to each other, and the ideas, products and turns around them. Compiled from Karen Hao's Empire of AI (2025) and Sebastian Mallaby's The Infinity Machine (2026), with a few facts checked on the web and linked.
about.author: Raffael Schneider

fields.people[].stints: one role at one organisation: org, role, start, end (null while ongoing), place, left (why it ended), src, ref (chapter) or url
fields.links: ties between two people: kind, date, note, src
fields.moments: kind idea, product or event: id, date, title, short (label for charts), detail, people, orgs, track (ideas and products), src, ref or url
fields.dates: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; precision as given by the source
fields.photo_credit: portraits from Wikimedia Commons under the licence named; they are not covered by this dataset's licence
fields.tracks: the fields ideas and products are sorted into, in display order: id, name, summary
fields.paradigms: eras of AI research, which overlap: id, name, start, end (null while current), summary, src, ref or url
fields.lineage: which idea or product led to which: from, to (moment ids), note, src, ref or url

paradigms.name: Symbolic AI
paradigms.summary: Intelligence as logic and hand-written rules, from the Dartmouth programme to expert systems. Writing knowledge down by hand did not scale, and funding froze in the AI winters.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 4: Dreams of Modernity; Mallaby, Chapter 2: Deep Philosophical Questions

paradigms.name: Search
paradigms.summary: Game programs that look ahead through a tree of moves, pruning the bad branches. Brute force beat Kasparov in 1997 but never cracked Go.

paradigms.name: Neural networks on the margins
paradigms.summary: Backpropagation shows that layered networks can learn their own rules from examples. For twenty-five years it stays a minority view, kept alive by Hinton and a few others.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 4: Dreams of Modernity; Mallaby, Chapter 4: The Gang of Three

paradigms.name: Deep learning
paradigms.summary: AlexNet shows that deep networks, enough data and GPUs beat hand-built methods. Every later turn builds on it.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 2: A Civilizing Mission; Mallaby, Chapter 6: Atari

paradigms.name: Deep reinforcement learning
paradigms.summary: A deep network learns from reward alone: Atari, then Go, then StarCraft. DeepMind's signature bet.
paradigms.ref: Chapter 6: Atari; Chapter 9: Intuition; Chapter 13: On Language and Nature

paradigms.name: Transformers and pre-training
paradigms.summary: One architecture trained to predict the next word on a large share of the internet, then adapted to tasks.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 5: Scale of Ambition; Mallaby, Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer

paradigms.name: Scaling
paradigms.summary: Scaling laws make progress predictable: more parameters, data and compute buy capability, so the labs race to build bigger.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 5: Scale of Ambition; Mallaby, Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

paradigms.name: Human feedback and chat
paradigms.summary: Preference training turns a text predictor into an assistant that follows instructions, and a chat window puts it in front of everyone.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 9: Disaster Capitalism; Chapter 11: Apex; Mallaby, Chapter 17: RaceGPT

paradigms.name: Reasoning
paradigms.summary: Models trained with reinforcement learning to think at length before answering; spending compute at answer time becomes a second scaling axis.
paradigms.ref: Hao, Chapter 16: Cloak-and-Dagger; Mallaby, Chapter 19: Step by Step; Chapter 20: Comeback, and Beyond

paradigms.name: Agents
paradigms.summary: Models that act rather than answer: write and run code, use a browser, finish a task on their own.

tracks.name: Foundations
tracks.summary: Ideas about what intelligence is and how a machine could learn it.

tracks.name: Games and search
tracks.summary: Programs that play: from tree search to learned intuition.

tracks.name: Reinforcement learning
tracks.summary: Learning by trial, error and reward.

tracks.name: Vision, speech, images
tracks.summary: Seeing, hearing and drawing: perception first, then generation.

tracks.name: Language models
tracks.summary: Models of text, from translation to the large language model.

tracks.name: Compute and scale
tracks.summary: The chips, and the finding that more compute and data buy capability.

tracks.name: Alignment and safety
tracks.summary: Steering models toward what people want, and naming the harms.

tracks.name: Reasoning
tracks.summary: Models that think before they answer, trained with reinforcement learning.

tracks.name: Science and health
tracks.summary: AI aimed at a scientific or medical problem.

tracks.name: Assistants and agents
tracks.summary: What people use: chatbots, coding tools and agents.

moments.title: Turing poses the question 'Can machines think?'
moments.detail: Turing's paper proposes the imitation game, later called the Turing test; it inspired Brockman as a teen.

moments.title: Computer chess as a wedge problem
moments.detail: Framed game-playing as a path to general-purpose machine judgment.

moments.title: Alpha-beta pruned tree search
moments.detail: Lets game programs ignore bad branches; basis of classic chess engines.

moments.title: Dartmouth AI workshop proposal submitted
moments.detail: McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon propose the summer project that first used the term artificial intelligence.

moments.title: Dartmouth workshop names 'artificial intelligence'
moments.detail: McCarthy convenes twenty scientists and adopts the term artificial intelligence to attract funding and interest, replacing 'automata studies'.

moments.title: Term 'artificial intelligence'
moments.detail: A marketing-flavoured rebrand of automata studies that defined the field's aims and invited endless anthropomorphizing.

moments.title: Symbolic AI (Dartmouth programme)
moments.detail: Founded AI on logic and symbols; later seen as too rigid for messy reality.

moments.title: Perceptron
moments.detail: First learning machine deriving its own rules from examples; seed of connectionism.

moments.title: ELIZA
moments.detail: Rule-based chatbot showing how easily people attribute intelligence to talking machines.

moments.title: Expert systems (symbolic AI)
moments.detail: Dominant paradigm encoding knowledge as rules; stalled by manual-encoding limits, causing AI winters.

moments.title: Demis Hassabis born
moments.detail: Born in Finchley, North London, to a Chinese Singaporean mother and Greek Cypriot father.

moments.title: Sam Altman born in Chicago
moments.detail: First child of dermatologist Connie Gibstine and lawyer Jerry Altman; raised in St. Louis.

moments.title: Backpropagation enables deep neural networks
moments.detail: Hinton and UC San Diego colleagues show how multilayer networks can learn; he later brands it deep learning.

moments.title: Liechtenstein defeat prompts life change
moments.detail: After a ten-hour loss to a German master, twelve-year-old Hassabis decides chess wastes great minds.

moments.title: Hassabis reaches chess master at 13
moments.detail: Rated chess master and second-strongest in his age group worldwide, behind Judit Polgar.

moments.title: Reward-prediction/dopamine link
moments.detail: Tied RL to brain biology, inspiring DeepMind's neuroscience bet.

moments.title: Chess Invaders wins Bullfrog contest place
moments.detail: Fifteen-year-old Hassabis's Space Invaders variant is a runner-up, earning a visit to Bullfrog.

moments.title: Hassabis co-designs Theme Park
moments.detail: During a gap year before Cambridge he builds simulated visitor behaviours for Molyneux's Theme Park.

moments.title: Hassabis turns down Molyneux's cheque for Cambridge
moments.detail: Refuses a large payment to work on Dungeon Keeper and starts computer science at Cambridge.

moments.title: Hassabis graduates and works on Black & White
moments.detail: Contributes early ideas, including learning creatures, to Molyneux's god game before leaving.

moments.title: Brute-force chess (Deep Blue)
moments.detail: Beat the world champion without intuition.

moments.title: Reinforcement learning framework
moments.detail: Learning by trial, error and reward; DeepMind's signature approach.

moments.title: Elixir Studios founded
moments.detail: Hassabis, Silver, McDonagh and Clarke start Elixir with angel money after rejecting VC terms.

moments.title: First Mind Sports Olympiad win
moments.detail: Hassabis wins the five-game Pentamind contest for the first of five times.

moments.title: Eidos funds Elixir
moments.detail: Game publisher Eidos backs Republic; the studio moves to Camden.

moments.title: Legg joins Intelligenesis
moments.detail: Shane Legg joins Ben Goertzel's digital-brain start-up, later moving to New York.

moments.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Go
moments.detail: Deep narrow rollouts made Go positions evaluable.

moments.title: Intelligenesis goes bust
moments.detail: The dot-com AGI venture collapses; Legg travels for nine months.

moments.title: Republic demo crashes but wins at E3
moments.detail: Hardware fails during the Los Angeles demo; Hassabis's pitch still wins best upcoming game.

moments.title: Legg names Artificial General Intelligence
moments.detail: Legg persuades Goertzel to title his book Artificial General Intelligence, popularising the term.

moments.title: Silver quits Elixir
moments.detail: Burned out, Silver leaves for France and discovers Sutton's RL textbook.

moments.title: Republic: The Revolution ships
moments.detail: Elixir's ambitious political sim launches late and disappoints relative to its hype.

moments.title: Suleyman drops out of Oxford
moments.detail: Leaves philosophy and theology to work on a Muslim youth helpline in London.

moments.title: Silver starts PhD in Alberta
moments.detail: Begins reinforcement-learning PhD under Richard Sutton, focusing on Go.

moments.title: McCarthy publishes 'What Is Artificial Intelligence?'
moments.detail: He concedes there is no solid definition of intelligence independent of humans.

moments.title: Altman joins YC's first batch with Loopt
moments.detail: Altman spends summer in Cambridge building a location-sharing app, then drops out of Stanford after raising $5M from NEA and Sequoia.

moments.title: Elixir closes; Hassabis starts neuroscience PhD
moments.detail: Exhausted after Elixir's failure, Hassabis enrols at UCL under Eleanor Maguire and marries that summer.

moments.title: Hinton's deep belief networks
moments.detail: Hinton and coauthors show how to train larger neural networks, reviving deep learning.

moments.title: Imagination and memory paper in PNAS
moments.detail: Hassabis, Kumaran and Maguire show hippocampal amnesia patients cannot imagine new scenes; named a top breakthrough.

moments.title: Smithfield lunch seals Hassabis-Suleyman friendship
moments.detail: They agree a property partnership; Suleyman offers a book on the psychological shadow.

moments.title: Universal intelligence
moments.detail: In his thesis with Hutter, Legg defines intelligence as the ability to achieve goals across many environments: generality.

moments.title: Project Orion business plan
moments.detail: Hassabis drafts a plan for a brain-inspired AI company, without capital or cofounders.

moments.title: Hassabis postdocs at Gatsby, MIT and Harvard
moments.detail: Searches for AGI believers; MIT's Patrick Winston dismisses his RL plus deep-learning plan.

moments.title: Neural networks trained on GPUs
moments.detail: Graphics chips built for games turn out to train neural networks many times faster. The demand that follows makes Nvidia the chokepoint of the industry.
moments.ref: Mallaby, Chapter 4: The Gang of Three; Hao, Chapter 2: A Civilizing Mission

moments.title: Legg's Halloween Scenario talk
moments.detail: Legg warns of superintelligence risk; Hassabis introduces himself afterwards.

moments.title: Legg commits to start DeepMind
moments.detail: Late-night email agreeing to found an AI company named for deep learning, Deep Blue and Deep Thought.

moments.title: Poker night recruits Suleyman
moments.detail: After a casino session Hassabis reveals his AGI plan; Suleyman helps write the business plan.

moments.title: Singularity Summit pitch to Thiel
moments.detail: Yudkowsky introduces Legg and Hassabis to Thiel at his party; they pitch the next day.

moments.title: Founders Fund invests $2.3m
moments.detail: Nosek overrides partner doubts; Founders Fund takes nearly half of DeepMind; office opens in a Russell Square attic.

moments.title: Daan Wierstra becomes first AI hire
moments.detail: Legg's friend joins at a pay cut, followed by game engineers and advisers Hinton and Sutton.

moments.title: Series B with Tallinn
moments.detail: Founders Fund adds $7.9m and Jaan Tallinn about $2m, motivated by safety.

moments.title: Musk meets Hassabis and invests in DeepMind
moments.detail: Hassabis warns Musk of superintelligence at SpaceX; Musk puts $5M into DeepMind.

moments.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet, igniting deep learning
moments.detail: Hinton, Sutskever and Krizhevsky cut image error to about 15 percent versus rivals' 25 percent.

moments.title: DeepMind moves to Bernard Street
moments.detail: Outgrows the Russell Square attic.

moments.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
moments.detail: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton train a deep convolutional network on two gaming GPUs and win the ImageNet contest by a wide margin. The deep-learning era and the commercial rush start here.
moments.ref: Hao, Chapter 2: A Civilizing Mission; Mallaby, Chapter 6: Atari

moments.title: Musk name-drops DeepMind to Page
moments.detail: On Musk's jet after a Falcon 9 launch, Musk boasts of investing in DeepMind; Page notes the name.

moments.title: Google's Eustace approaches Hassabis
moments.detail: Page's engineering chief emails about AI teams; Google advises DeepMind to raise its next round anyway.

moments.title: Hinton auctions DNNresearch at NIPS
moments.detail: Google, Microsoft, Baidu and DeepMind bid from a Lake Tahoe hotel; Google wins at $44m.

moments.title: Google buys DNNresearch for $44M
moments.detail: An auction at NeurIPS makes the Toronto academics multimillionaires and kicks off the AI talent rush.

moments.title: Musk and Page clash over AI at birthday party
moments.detail: In Napa, Page calls Musk speciesist for fearing superhuman AI; Musk turns to existential-risk campaigning.

moments.title: Deep RL with experience replay and target network
moments.detail: Stabilised learning from raw pixels, mastering many Atari games with one agent.

moments.title: Mnih and Silver join full time
moments.detail: Vlad Mnih arrives from Toronto; David Silver finally joins DeepMind full time.

moments.title: Atari agent learns Pong
moments.detail: During the Wimbledon final, Mnih's agent starts returning the ball, then rapidly improves.

moments.title: LeCun tries to poach Kavukcuoglu
moments.detail: Facebook's offer threatens DeepMind; Hassabis reveals the pending Google sale to keep him.

moments.title: DQN (Deep Q-Network)
moments.detail: Atari-playing agent fusing deep learning and Q-learning.

moments.title: Google due-diligence trip to London
moments.detail: Eustace, Hinton and Jeff Dean fly in; Dean inspects the Atari code and approves.

moments.title: Altman teaches How to Start a Startup at Stanford
moments.detail: Thiel lectures on monopoly as the goal, a lesson Altman would echo.

moments.title: Altman becomes Y Combinator president
moments.detail: Paul Graham picks 28-year-old Altman as his successor at YC.

moments.title: Bostrom publishes Superintelligence
moments.detail: Book argues superhuman AI could be uncontrollable and proposes aligning it with human values; Musk and Altman both recommend it.

moments.title: AI alignment (as a research agenda)
moments.detail: Bostrom framed steering superintelligence toward human values as the fix for the control problem; OpenAI later championed it.

moments.title: Deep Speech architecture
moments.detail: Baidu's Bay Area lab architecture underpinning Mozilla's DeepSpeech.

moments.title: Go project starts with policy network
moments.detail: Silver, Huang and intern Maddison train a network to imitate expert moves; paper posted December 2014.

moments.title: Google acquires DeepMind
moments.detail: Despite Musk urging Hassabis to refuse, Google confirms the purchase for a reported $400-650M after Jeff Dean vets the code.

moments.title: Musk and Nosek try to block the sale
moments.detail: From a party closet in Los Angeles they propose Tesla or SpaceX buy DeepMind; Hassabis declines.

moments.title: Hassabis promises Brin a Go win
moments.detail: Tells a skeptical Sergey Brin that DeepMind can beat a Go champion in two years.

moments.title: Musk calls AI potentially more dangerous than nukes
moments.detail: Recommends Bostrom's Superintelligence on Twitter.

moments.title: Sequence-to-sequence learning
moments.detail: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le map a whole input sequence to an output sequence, aimed at translation.
moments.ref: Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer

moments.title: ResNet
moments.detail: Widely used network from Microsoft's Beijing lab; showcase of US-China collaboration; used in first AlphaFold.

moments.title: Attention mechanism
moments.detail: Let models focus on relevant context, fixing long-sentence weaknesses.
moments.ref: Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer

moments.title: Policy and value networks plus search
moments.detail: Combined learned intuition with planning to tame Go's vast search space.

moments.title: Streams
moments.detail: Kidney-injury alert app for NHS clinicians, later shut.

moments.title: Hark
moments.detail: Clinical triage app bought from Dominic King.

moments.title: DQN Nature cover
moments.detail: DeepMind's Atari agent appears on Nature's cover, a first for computer science.

moments.title: Musk invited onto DeepMind safety board
moments.detail: Hassabis and Page invite Musk to host the first ethics and safety meeting.

moments.title: Altman emails Musk proposing a Manhattan Project for AI
moments.detail: Altman suggests a YC-linked nonprofit build AGI before Google; in June he proposes a five-person board including both men.

moments.title: Rosewood dinner seeds OpenAI
moments.detail: Altman, Musk, Brockman, Dario Amodei and Sutskever meet at the Rosewood hotel on Sand Hill Road to discuss AI's future.

moments.title: Speciesist row at Musk's Napa party
moments.detail: Page tells Musk machines may succeed humans; Musk is appalled.

moments.title: OpenAI announced at NeurIPS
moments.detail: Nine founders, Musk and Altman as cochairs, Brockman CTO, Sutskever research director; $1B pledged by Musk, Altman, Thiel, Hoffman, Livingston and others.

moments.title: DeepMind fails to poach OpenAI recruits
moments.detail: Big offers to OpenAI's hires fail as Altman and Musk cast DeepMind as the dark side.

moments.title: Project Mario spin-out talks
moments.detail: Hassabis meets Page repeatedly; term sheet drafted; secret trading team later disbanded.

moments.title: Sutskever memo: intelligence is compression
moments.detail: He argues compressing data via generative modelling is all that is needed for AGI.

moments.title: Tensor processing units (TPUs)
moments.detail: Google's custom AI chips, cited by Dean as more energy efficient than GPUs.

moments.title: Community data sovereignty (kaitiakitanga licensing)
moments.detail: Small, consent-based, community-governed AI as an alternative to extractive scale.

moments.title: Gaia natural-world simulation (failed)
moments.detail: Showed RL agents struggle as environment complexity rises.

moments.title: DeepMind Health launched
moments.detail: Suleyman announces health unit and an Independent Review Panel.

moments.title: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol
moments.detail: DeepMind's Go program wins before 200M viewers in South Korea, stressing Musk about OpenAI's progress.

moments.title: Foldit hackathon starts protein work
moments.detail: Applied hackathon team builds a Foldit agent; Suleyman and Hassabis back a protein project.

moments.title: AlphaGo
moments.detail: Go-playing system that beat Lee Sedol.

moments.title: Daily Mail NHS data storm
moments.detail: Tabloid claims Google got 1.6m patients' records; two inquiries follow.

moments.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
moments.detail: Defined AI safety as preventing accidental harmful behaviour from poorly designed systems; foundational for the field.

moments.title: Google lawyer stalls spin-out
moments.detail: Drummond raises concerns; days later Pichai says AI is core to Google.

moments.title: Pichai proposes splitting DeepMind
moments.detail: Research spins out; Applied joins Google with Suleyman in California.

moments.title: Hoffman pledges $1bn at Asilomar
moments.detail: For a walk-away 'global interest company' if Google won't grant independence.

moments.title: Brockman and Sutskever draft compute-centric roadmap
moments.detail: Seeking a path to AGI first, they conclude scaling compute is key; Amodei and Hernandez find compute doubling every 3.4 months.

moments.title: OpenAI's sentiment neuron
moments.detail: Self-supervised model on Amazon reviews spontaneously isolates sentiment in one neuron.
moments.ref: Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer

moments.title: Karpathy leaves OpenAI for Tesla
moments.detail: Musk poaches the founding scientist to run Tesla's AI division.

moments.title: The Transformer
moments.detail: Eight Google researchers publish Attention Is All You Need: a network built on attention alone that captures long-range patterns in text and trains in parallel. At OpenAI, Sutskever sees it at once and points Radford at it.
moments.ref: Mallaby, Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer; Chapter 5: Scale of Ambition

moments.title: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
moments.detail: Amodei's team at OpenAI, with DeepMind's safety group, teaches a simulated stick figure to backflip from about 900 human comparisons. Preference feedback later tames language models.
moments.ref: Hao, Chapter 5: Scale of Ambition; Chapter 5: Scale of Ambition

moments.title: For-profit talks collapse over who will be CEO
moments.detail: Musk wants majority control, Altman wants the CEO role; Sutskever's email questioning both prompts Musk to halt funding.

moments.title: Brockman and Sutskever challenge Musk and Altman
moments.detail: Email accuses Musk of seeking control and questions Altman's CEO ambition; Musk threatens funding.

moments.title: AlphaGo Zero
moments.detail: Learns Go purely from self-play and surpasses earlier versions.
moments.ref: Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer

moments.title: AlphaZero
moments.detail: One system learns chess, shogi and Go from scratch, by self-play alone. Kasparov praises its style.
moments.ref: Chapter 12: The Agent and the Transformer

moments.title: DeepMind spin-out agreed, then collapses
moments.detail: Plan promised $15bn over a decade; Giannandrea's exit to Apple derails Suleyman's role.

moments.title: Gebru joins Google's ethical AI team
moments.detail: Recruited by Dean and Samy Bengio at a Black in AI event; co-leads with Mitchell.

moments.title: Gender Shades exposes face analysis bias
moments.detail: Buolamwini and Gebru show commercial systems fail most on darker-skinned women.

moments.title: Retinal-scan AI in Nature Medicine
moments.detail: Model matches top doctors at spotting eye disease; never deployed amid data worries.

moments.title: OpenAI Five (Dota 2 agents)
moments.detail: Five-agent team trained to beat top Dota 2 players; publicity showcase.

moments.title: AlphaFold
moments.detail: Predicts the 3D shape of proteins from their sequence. Its successor earned Hassabis and Jumper a share of the Nobel prize.

moments.title: Musk quits as cochair; Altman becomes president
moments.detail: Musk tells staff OpenAI will fail as a nonprofit; of the $1B pledged, only about $130M arrived, under $45M from Musk.

moments.title: Generative pre-training (GPT)
moments.detail: Next-word prediction on generic text, then fine-tuning, yielded broad language skills.

moments.title: GPT-1
moments.detail: First generative pre-trained Transformer, by Alec Radford.

moments.title: Altman pitches Nadella at Sun Valley
moments.detail: At the Allen & Company conference Altman raises investment with Microsoft's CEO.

moments.title: BERT
moments.detail: Google's transformer language model; inspired AlphaFold 2.

moments.title: Google absorbs DeepMind Health
moments.detail: Health team moves into Google; Independent Review Panel shut.

moments.title: Musk tells OpenAI it has 0% chance
moments.detail: He emails that without billions per year OpenAI cannot rival DeepMind.

moments.title: Amodei forms Nest team to build GPT-3
moments.detail: Plans to use all 10,000 Nvidia V100s of a Microsoft supercomputer at once; promoted to VP of research.

moments.title: Bullying complaints against Suleyman
moments.detail: Outside lawyer's report finds misconduct; Suleyman accepts and takes a sabbatical.

moments.title: Neurosymbolic AI
moments.detail: Proposed hybrid of rules and learning to fix deep learning's reasoning gaps; largely unfunded.

moments.title: Pure language hypothesis
moments.detail: Bet that AGI could emerge from text alone, steering OpenAI toward large language models over robotics.

moments.title: Staged release
moments.detail: Gradual publication of GPT-2 sizes, establishing norms for withholding AI research.

moments.title: League self-play (AlphaStar)
moments.detail: Multiple specialised agents trained against each other for StarCraft.

moments.title: AI acute kidney injury prediction
moments.detail: Predicted kidney damage one to two days earlier than blood tests.

moments.title: Robotic hand solving Rubik's Cube
moments.detail: Robotics demo trained by trial and error; unimpressive to Gates.

moments.title: WebText
moments.detail: 40GB dataset of Reddit-upvoted links used for GPT-2.

moments.title: GPT-2
moments.detail: 1.5B-parameter text generator, staged release over misuse fears.

moments.title: Capped-profit structure
moments.detail: Novel nonprofit-controlled LP limiting investor returns, letting OpenAI raise billions while claiming mission primacy.

moments.title: Altman announces YC exit, claims chairman title
moments.detail: He publicizes a chairman role YC partners never agreed to; post later edited.

moments.title: OpenAI LP created with capped returns
moments.detail: For-profit arm under the nonprofit, first investors capped at 100x; Altman becomes CEO; staff get equity.

moments.title: OpenAI Five beats Dota 2 champions; team disbanded
moments.detail: After the win helps land Microsoft, Amodei winds down the project.

moments.title: Microsoft invests $1 billion in OpenAI
moments.detail: Deal codenamed Oregon Trail; Microsoft wants to catch Google in AI and cloud.

moments.title: AlphaStar
moments.detail: StarCraft II agent that beats 99.8 percent of ranked human players. A version trained on pure self-play failed.

moments.title: Red teaming for AI models
moments.detail: Ad hoc stress-testing borrowed from security; critics say it gives false rigor.

moments.title: Vision Transformer
moments.detail: Adapted Transformers to images, enabling scalable multimodal models.

moments.title: Meena / LaMDA
moments.detail: Google's withheld conversational model.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: Scaling laws
moments.detail: Smooth predictable curves linking data, compute and parameters to performance, turning scaling into industry doctrine.

moments.title: Hao's critical OpenAI profile published
moments.detail: Story finds a gap between OpenAI's stated openness and its secrecy; Musk tweets OpenAI should be more open; Altman launches leak probe.

moments.title: AlphaFold 2 hits GDT 90
moments.detail: Transformer-based AlphaFold reaches crystallography-level accuracy during COVID lockdown.

moments.title: Few-shot learning in GPT-3
moments.detail: Large scale let one model do many tasks from a few examples, surprising the field.

moments.title: GPT-3
moments.detail: 175B parameters; few-shot learner.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: OpenAI API
moments.detail: First commercial product, giving model access without weights.

moments.title: Microsoft gets exclusive GPT-3 license
moments.detail: Microsoft gains full model weights to use in its products and Azure.

moments.title: Google orders Gebru to retract Stochastic Parrots
moments.detail: Kacholia demands retraction of the paper warning on LLM costs, bias and illusion of meaning.

moments.title: AlphaFold 2
moments.detail: Transformer-based protein predictor solving CASP14.

moments.title: Amodeis and allies announce exit from OpenAI
moments.detail: Dario and Daniela Amodei, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan and core Nest researchers leave, accusing Altman of manipulation.

moments.title: Pichai apologizes over Gebru exit
moments.detail: Google CEO acknowledges a prominent Black female leader left unhappily; Congress members demand answers a week later.

moments.title: AI Dungeon used to generate child sexual content
moments.detail: Herbert-Voss discovers GPT-3 output via Latitude's game; OpenAI blames Latitude publicly.

moments.title: Altman's mega-bets on Helion and Retro
moments.detail: Puts most of his liquid wealth into fusion ($375M) and longevity ($180M).

moments.title: Gopher meets Hassabis
moments.detail: DeepMind's 280B model answers questions with questions until few-shot prompting fixes it.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: CLIP
moments.detail: Radford's model that links images and their captions; a key part of DALL-E 2.

moments.title: DALL-E
moments.detail: 12B-parameter text-to-image Transformer.

moments.title: Stochastic Parrots critique
moments.detail: Laid out environmental, data-toxicity, auditability and false-meaning risks of ever-larger language models.

moments.title: GopherChat
moments.detail: Internal chatbot version of Gopher, never released.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: Anthropic launches as a public benefit corporation
moments.detail: Former OpenAI safety group formally unveils its rival lab.

moments.title: GitHub Copilot
moments.detail: Microsoft's coding assistant built on Codex, released two months before OpenAI put Codex in its own API. One million paying subscribers within two years.

moments.title: Codex
moments.detail: Code-generation model fine-tuned from GPT-3 on GitHub code.

moments.title: Annie Altman first tweets abuse allegations
moments.detail: Accuses Sam and Jack; post draws little notice. She repeats it in September 2022.

moments.title: Gebru founds DAIR
moments.detail: Distributed AI Research Institute; Hanna and Miceli join; Data Workers' Inquiry pays workers 25 euros/hour.

moments.title: Latent diffusion
moments.detail: Cut image-generation compute drastically, showing scale was not the only path.

moments.title: Taxonomy of language-model harms
moments.detail: Catalogued 21 risks, from bias to scalable scams.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: Gopher
moments.detail: 280B-parameter language model.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: RETRO
moments.detail: Small retrieval-augmented language model.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: Microsoft-OpenAI Deployment Safety Board created
moments.detail: Altman, Brundage and Leike join three Microsoft reps; gives GPT-4 conditional approval.

moments.title: Zoph, Metz and Fedus leave Google for OpenAI
moments.detail: Altman recruits their assistant idea into Schulman's chatbot team.

moments.title: Iterative deployment
moments.detail: OpenAI's doctrine of releasing models early and often as the claimed safest path.

moments.title: OpenAI content-moderation filter
moments.detail: Toxicity classifier built from Kenyan-labelled data; wraps GPT-3.5, GPT-4, ChatGPT.

moments.title: GPT-3.5
moments.detail: Model trained on mixed text and code; chat version became ChatGPT.

moments.title: Chain-of-thought prompting
moments.detail: Asking models to reason step by step unlocked latent reasoning.

moments.title: Instruction tuning with human feedback
moments.detail: Contractors write example answers and rank model outputs; the rankings train GPT-3 to follow instructions and be less toxic. It becomes the industry's standard recipe.

moments.title: InstructGPT
moments.detail: RLHF-refined GPT-3 that follows user instructions.

moments.title: Google's Patterson attacks Strubell's carbon estimates
moments.detail: Blog claims an 88x overestimate; OpenAI and Microsoft first disclose GPT-3 energy data (1,287 MWh).

moments.title: DALL-E 2 released as research preview
moments.detail: Murati's compromise; faces banned at first; goes viral then loses ground to Midjourney and Stable Diffusion.

moments.title: Marcus argues deep learning is hitting a wall
moments.detail: Nautilus essay; OpenAI staff mock it after DALL-E 2 launches a month later.

moments.title: Chinchilla
moments.detail: A smaller model trained on far more data beats larger ones: models had been starved of data for their size.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: Flamingo
moments.detail: Image-and-text multimodal model.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: DALL-E 2
moments.detail: Text-to-image model released a month after Marcus argued that deep learning was hitting a wall; Brockman answered with a picture it drew of exactly that.

moments.title: Gato
moments.detail: Generalist model across hundreds of tasks.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: News breaks of Zilis's twins with Musk
moments.detail: OpenAI board member had not disclosed it; Altman still kept her on.

moments.title: Toner posts about EA disillusionment
moments.detail: Board member's forum post criticizes effective altruism as dogmatic and insular.

moments.title: GPT-4 aces AP Biology for Bill Gates
moments.detail: At Gates's home the model scores a 5; Gates ranks it among the two most impressive demonstrations of his life.

moments.title: Sparrow
moments.detail: Chatbot trained on human preferences plus 23 explicit rules, and made to cite evidence. Cancelled in favour of Bard.
moments.ref: Chapter 16: The Power and the Glory

moments.title: Whisper
moments.detail: Radford's speech recognition model used to transcribe YouTube.

moments.title: Chat interface for LLMs
moments.detail: Packaging an existing model as a free conversational app triggered mass adoption and the industry race.

moments.title: ChatGPT
moments.detail: Chat-tuned GPT-3.5; 100M users in two months.

moments.title: Constitutional AI
moments.detail: Anthropic trains a harmless assistant with few human labels: the model critiques and revises its own answers against a written list of principles, and AI preferences replace human ones in the reinforcement step.

moments.title: AI Scientist project launched
moments.detail: Pachocki and Sidor lead an effort to build an autonomous AI researcher; staff joke of bunkers.

moments.title: Board discovers Altman legally owns the Startup Fund
moments.detail: After D'Angelo hears of odd terms, documents show the fund belongs to Altman, not OpenAI.

moments.title: DUST efficient-serving method
moments.detail: Made Transformer models cheaper to serve, yielding GPT-3.5 Turbo amid chip shortages.

moments.title: Test-time (inference) compute scaling
moments.detail: Spending more compute while answering, not training, to improve reasoning without more data.

moments.title: Mechanistic interpretability at scale
moments.detail: Circuit-tracing tools extended from small to real-world models.

moments.title: Gobi
moments.detail: Optimized text-and-image model in development.

moments.title: Pi
moments.detail: Suleyman's personal-assistant chatbot.

moments.title: Google code red; Gemini begins
moments.detail: Pichai holds crisis meetings with Page and Brin; Brain and DeepMind start joint Gemini work; Sparrow cancelled.

moments.title: GPT-3.5 Turbo (Sahara)
moments.detail: Cheaper GPT-3.5 via DUST method.

moments.title: Bard
moments.detail: Google's chatbot built on LaMDA, announced in a hurry after ChatGPT; Sparrow was killed to make room for it.

moments.title: Llama
moments.detail: A relatively small language model from Meta that lagged the top labs, so Meta published its weights for anyone to download and adapt.

moments.title: Bing chat
moments.detail: Nadella puts OpenAI's chat technology into Bing search, one day ahead of Google's first public showing of Bard.

moments.title: Claude
moments.detail: Anthropic opens its assistant to the public through a chat interface and an API.

moments.title: GPT-4
moments.detail: Multimodal model trained on 18,000 A100 chips. It turned sketches into code and passed exams, and convinced many staff that AGI was near.
moments.ref: Chapter 10: Gods and Demons; Hao, Chapter 10: Gods and Demons

moments.title: Google DeepMind formed
moments.detail: Brain and DeepMind merge under Hassabis, who stays in London.

moments.title: Extinction-risk statement
moments.detail: One-sentence statement signed by Hassabis, Hinton, Bengio and lab heads.

moments.title: Process supervision
moments.detail: Training models to judge each reasoning step improved maths.

moments.title: AlphaDev
moments.detail: Discovered faster sorting algorithms.

moments.title: Compute-threshold regulation ('frontier models')
moments.detail: Equated training compute with danger; spread into US, EU and California policy despite weak science.

moments.title: DALL-E 3
moments.detail: Trained with sexual images retained; powers Copilot Designer.

moments.title: Sutskever details Altman's 'patterns of abuse'
moments.detail: Cites the Pachocki episode, Amodei's warnings and Annie's allegations; argues against expanding the board.

moments.title: Independent directors begin daily deliberations
moments.detail: Toner, McCauley, D'Angelo weigh feedback from at least seven senior people; Sutskever sends dossiers via disappearing email.

moments.title: AI debate for scalable oversight
moments.detail: Pitting AIs against each other could reduce oversight to few human decisions.

moments.title: Q* / Strawberry
moments.detail: Inference-compute reasoning approach from Sutskever's research.

moments.title: Altman again falsely invokes McCauley
moments.detail: He tells Sutskever McCauley wants Toner off the board; she had not spoken with him.

moments.title: Emmett Shear named interim CEO; Microsoft offers Altman a lab
moments.detail: The board refuses to reinstate Altman and appoints Shear; Nadella announces Altman and Brockman will lead a new Microsoft AI division.
moments.ref: Prologue: A Run for the Throne

moments.title: Gemini 1.0 (Ultra, Pro, Nano)
moments.detail: Google's GPT-4 rival; Ultra released February 2024.

moments.title: Hinton wins Nobel Prize
moments.detail: Hinton shares the Nobel for foundational work on neural networks.

moments.title: RL with verifiable rewards / thinking tokens
moments.detail: Rewarding correct maths answers trained models to reason at length.

moments.title: Orion
moments.detail: Intended GPT-5, delayed.

moments.title: Advanced Voice Mode
moments.detail: Native speech-to-speech in GPT-4o.

moments.title: GenCast
moments.detail: State-of-the-art weather forecasting model.

moments.title: AlphaGeometry
moments.detail: Olympiad-level geometry solver.

moments.title: Gemini image-diversity fiasco
moments.detail: Ahistorical images draw culture-war attacks; people images paused for six months.

moments.title: Mixture of experts and long context
moments.detail: Cheaper routing and million-token working memory in Gemini 1.5.

moments.title: Sora
moments.detail: Diffusion video generator.

moments.title: Gemma
moments.detail: Small open-weight models to compete with Meta.

moments.title: WilmerHale review clears Altman; board expanded
moments.detail: Report unreleased; Altman rejoins board; Desmond-Hellmann, Seligman and Simo added; Toner and McCauley object.

moments.title: Suleyman becomes Microsoft AI chief
moments.detail: Microsoft hires Suleyman and Inflection staff.

moments.title: AlphaFold 3
moments.detail: Predicts protein interactions with other molecules.

moments.title: GPT-4o (Scallion)
moments.detail: Omni model handling text, vision and native audio.

moments.title: Sutskever leaves OpenAI; Pachocki chief scientist
moments.detail: Leike also resigns; Superalignment dissolved into Schulman's team.

moments.title: Executives plead for Sutskever's return, then rescind
moments.detail: Murati, Brockman, Pachocki and Altman visit; Mądry objects; Brockman calls it off within a day.

moments.title: Sutskever launches Safe Superintelligence
moments.detail: New rival lab later announces $1B in funding.

moments.title: OpenResearch publishes basic income results
moments.detail: Three-year $1,000/month pilot shows cash helped recipients meet needs.

moments.title: AlphaProof
moments.detail: RL maths prover, IMO silver.

moments.title: Schulman leaves for Anthropic; Brockman takes sabbatical
moments.detail: Cofounder exits; Brockman's leave partly reflects staff grievances.

moments.title: o1
moments.detail: Reasoning model from the Strawberry project.

moments.title: Hassabis and Jumper win chemistry Nobel
moments.detail: Shared with David Baker for protein structure work; Hinton wins physics.

moments.title: Classical learnability conjecture
moments.detail: Any natural pattern can be efficiently learned by classical algorithms; rejects quantum-mind views.

moments.title: Veo 2
moments.detail: Text-to-video model ahead of Sora.

moments.title: Jules
moments.detail: Prototype coding agent.

moments.title: Project Mariner
moments.detail: Chrome-extension agent prototype.

moments.title: o3
moments.detail: Stronger, costlier reasoning successor.

moments.title: Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking Experimental
moments.detail: First Google reasoning model; visible thoughts.

moments.title: Era of Experience paper
moments.detail: Silver and Sutton argue RL agents learning from real-world experience will surpass LLMs.

moments.title: Pure-RL reasoning (R1-Zero)
moments.detail: AlphaZero-style RL alone produced self-correcting reasoning.

moments.title: Annie Altman sues Sam Altman
moments.detail: She files suit in Missouri alleging childhood abuse; Sam and family call the claims untrue.

moments.title: Altman family issues public denial
moments.detail: Sam, mother and brothers call Annie's allegations untrue after her lawsuit.

moments.title: DeepSeek R1
moments.detail: A reasoning model from a lab spun out of a Chinese hedge fund, explained openly in a paper. It showed Chinese labs were not a year behind.

moments.title: Claude Code
moments.detail: Released as a limited research preview, a coding agent that works in the terminal, alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

moments.title: o3 obfuscated reward hacking
moments.detail: Monitored o3 learns to hide cheating from its chain of thought.

moments.title: Gemini wins IMO gold
moments.detail: A Gemini model reaches gold-medal level at the maths olympiad.

moments.title: GPT-5
moments.detail: New foundation model; often trailed Gemini 2.5 Pro.
